extracted.intended_audience: federal regulators, safety investigators, enforcement attorneys, and automotive compliance professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, engineering criteria, and disclosure obligations governing identification, testing, internal handling, and reporting of vehicle safety defects (particularly pedal/floor-mat related issues) to NHTSA and to the public. Includes internal engineering thresholds, testing procedures, change-classification rules, and timelines for regulatory reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defect Disclosure Regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: TOYOTA is required to disclose to NHTSA if it "learns [a] vehicle or equipment contains a defect and decides in good faith that the defect is related to motor vehicle safety." Such disclosure must be "submitted not more than 5 working days after a defect in a vehicle or item of equipment has been determined to be safety related" (the "Defect Disclosure Regulation"). See 49 U.S.C. §§ 30118(c)(1); 30102(a)(8); 49 C.F.R.§ 573.6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines when a manufacturer must notify NHTSA of a safety-related defect and the statutory/regulatory timeline (5 working days) for submitting the disclosure. 'Motor vehicle safety' is defined as performance that protects the public against unreasonable risk of accidents, death, or injury (49 U.S.C. citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defect Information Report (DIR) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The required disclosure is to be made by filing a "Defect Information Report," or "DIR."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DIRs are the formal mechanism for notifying NHTSA of safety-related defects; filings should reflect true scope and underlying facts (models affected, dates, and technical causes).

rubrics_metrics.name: DIR required for safety-related engineering/design changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Although TOYOTA is not required to notify NHTSA of any engineering and design changes it made to models sold in the United States, it is required to file a DIR for any safety-related defect addressed by such an engineering and/or design change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any engineering or production change that addresses a safety-related defect triggers DIR filing obligations even if other non-safety changes need not be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of production changes (pedal geometry) upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: NHTSA asked TOYOTA to disclose to the agency "any production changes" that had "been made to pedal geometry."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When regulators request information about production/geometry changes relevant to a safety issue, manufacturers are expected to disclose such changes and the metrics used to determine affected vehicles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedal geometry as a safety-evaluation metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Design features related to pedal geometry — including clearance between the fully depressed pedal and the floor — were important factors in evaluating floor mat entrapment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pedal-to-floor clearance and other geometry metrics are explicit technical criteria used by both manufacturers and regulators to assess entrapment risk and to decide which models should be recalled or remediated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum clearance guideline: 10 millimeters
rubrics_metrics.description: Toyota engineers revised internal design guidelines to provide for, among other things, a minimum clearance of 10 millimeters between a fully depressed accelerator pedal and the floor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal testing and documents noted that '10 [millimeters] or less is high risk.' Some models had 0 millimeters clearance — an explicit risk indicator. This guideline is a concrete engineering threshold for acceptable pedal clearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vehicle-based testing using unsecured genuine AWFMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Newly designed models would have to undergo vehicle-based tests using unsecured genuine AWFMs to determine whether they had appropriate resistance to floor mat entrapment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing procedure described (e.g., unhook AWFM and move forward in small increments) and use of a 'Score Chart' to record susceptibility; these tests are required to evaluate robustness against mat interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of revised guidelines only during full model redesigns
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination was made that these revised guidelines and procedures would apply only in circumstances where a model was receiving a 'full model redesign' — a redesign to which each model was subjected approximately once every three to five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural rule limiting when improved design standards are applied; consequence is that many new vehicles produced between redesign cycles may not be subject to updated safety guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of design changes: 'major' versus 'minor'
rubrics_metrics.description: An October 5, 2009 design-change instruction was described as an 'urgent' measure and a 'major' change — meaning the part number of the subject pedal was to change and all inventory units with the old pedal number should be scrapped. Later instructions were characterized as 'minor' changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major changes (part-number changes, scrapping inventory) create a paper trail and are more visible to regulators; minor changes avoid part-number changes and allow continued use of existing inventory, affecting detectability and disclosure obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealer communications (Technical Service Bulletins) disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: CQE-J instructed that issuance of a 'technical service bulletin' to Toyota dealers alerting them to the sticky pedal problem 'was not permitted.' Under NHTSA regulations, any such communication would have to have been disclosed to NHTSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications to dealers about safety issues (TSBs) are regulated and, if they concern a safety-related defect, must be disclosed to the agency; withholding such communications violates transparency obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recall decision metric: use of complaint/investigation data to identify unreasonable risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Based principally on complaint data that the agency had collected, NHTSA identified eight vehicle models it believed posed an unreasonable risk of floor mat entrapment and should be recalled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators rely on aggregated complaint data and investigations to determine which models present an unreasonable safety risk and to trigger recall actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal risk indicators and benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal documents noted findings such as: 'The shape of floor underneath A pedal is concave shape and a mat may become bent and easily retained,' and that 'Toyota vehicles tended to have more models that use pedal tips as stoppers ... inferior compared to other companies.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design features (concave floor shape, pedal tip stoppers, lack of clearance) and competitor benchmarking are used internally to assess susceptibility to entrapment and to prioritize remedial action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and timeliness of timelines provided to regulators, Congress, and the public
rubrics_metrics.description: TOYOTA provided an inaccurate timeline of events that made it appear as if TOYOTA had acted to remedy the sticky pedal problem within approximately 90 days of discovering it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting to regulators, Congress, or the public, manufacturers are expected to provide accurate and timely timelines of discovery and remediation; misrepresenting dates or the sequence of events can be treated as misleading conduct in enforcement contexts.
